newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Seven sees tax expense start in 96/7.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Seven sees tax expense start in 96/7.

text.p: Television broadcaster The Seven Network Ltd said on Monday it expected to begin paying full income tax expenses in the current year to June 30, 1997.
It also said there was scope for further improvement in ratings and revenues.
"It is anticipated that full income tax expense will commence in the 1996/97 financial year," Seven said in releasing its annual results for 1995/96.
"This year's (A$3.29 million) tax expense is a concequence of the company's acquisition of Sunshine Broadcasting," Seven said.

Earlier Seven said its pre-tax operating profit rose 35.5 percent to A$119.96 million in 1995/96 and its net profit rose to A$115.13 million from A$41.26 million after an abnormal loss of A$1.35 million. Analysts had expected net profit to be around A$114 million pre-abnormals.
Seven said its sales on a comparable 52 week basis rose 13.1 percent for the year, while its EBIT (earnings before interest and tax) to sales ratio improved 19 percent to 19.7 percent.
Seven set a 13 cents per share final dividend, taking the total dividend to 17.5 cents versus 16.5 cents a year earlier.
Seven Managing Director Gary Rice said there was room for ratings improvements at Seven's free-to-air broadcasting arm.
"There is scope for the further improvement of our free-to-air business in ratings and revenue," Rice said.
"While we will continue to pursue opportunities which will grow the company, our principal focus remains the strengthening of the network," he said.
Rice said Seven had aimed to further strengthen its news and current affairs programming during the year.
"Our presence in news and current affairs is a long term project," he said.
The signing of a long term agreement with the International Olympic Committee and new Australian programming were also designed to improve the core broadcast television business, he said.
